newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka army says encircling rebel stronghold.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka army says encircling rebel stronghold.

text.p: Sri Lankan security forces have almost encircled the northern Tamil Tigers' stronghold of Kilinochchi, the last major town under rebel control, a military official said on Sunday.
"We're on the verge of encircling Kilinochchi," the official said.

Military officials said Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels had overrun a remote police post killing 15 members of the security forces on Sunday in a bid to distract the army from its assault on Kilinochchi.

Western aid workers said civilian casualties in the battle for Kilinochchi town, in which the military said more than 800 soldiers and rebels had been killed in the past week, were mounting and that they were running short of drugs.

Troops, backed by tanks, artillery and air support, advancing on the western flank of the pincer move, were well to the south of the town and were moving to cut the main road leading from it, the military official said.
On the eastern flank, troops were consolidating positions captured from the LTTE during the week-long offensive.

A third column of troops on Saturday began advancing from Paranthan, the launch pad of the offensive, on the main road which runs through Kilinochchi and met heavy rebel resistance after about one kilometre (half a mile), he said.
Ground troops confirmed killing 35 rebels and wounding about 50 on Saturday, while 10 soldiers were killed and 43, including an officer, were wounded, the official said.
A large rebel force attacked the Wanela post protecting a village, about 28 km (17 miles) from the eastern port of Trincomalee, early on Sunday, the military said.
"The post was destroyed," said an official. "Twelve para-military homeguards and three police constables were killed."
Military officials said they expected the rebels to step up attacks in the east to try to divert the army's attention from its assault on Kilinochchi, 285 km (180 miles) north of Colombo.
"They'll try their best to get us to divert troops from the offensive to guard border villages," a military official said.
Aid teams near Kilinochchi reported the area to be quiet on Sunday morning.
The Tigers set up base in Kilinochchi in April after the army captured their northern Jaffna peninsula stronghold, which they had ruled for almost a decade.
The Defence Ministry has said about 625 rebels have been killed and more than 650 wounded while the army has lost 219 soldiers in the assault on Kilinochchi. Nearly 300 soldiers have been wounded.
The rebels have offered stiff resistance with heavy rocket-propelled grenade and mortar fire, the military said.
The rebels on Friday blew up a telecommunications tower in Kilinochchi in a move defence analysts said could mean they were planning to pull out of the town.
The Tigers, fighting for independence in the Indian Ocean island's north and east, accused the army of exaggerating LTTE losses to divert attention from its own heavy casualties.
"More than 150 soldiers were killed and more than 200 wounded when LTTE forces launched an attack on Sri Lankan armed forces," the LTTE said of battles on Thursday in a statement faxed to Reuters.
It was not possible to verify the claims as the government has banned journalists from visiting the war zone.
Western aid officials said medical centres run by non-governmental organisations were short of drugs to treat civilians wounded in the fighting.
"It is difficult for our team to work because of a shortage of medical supplies." said a spokeswoman for a Western aid agency operating south of Kilinochchi.
